claim: Spatial Perturb-Seq was reported to jointly recover CRISPR perturbation identity, whole-transcriptome state, spatial location, and microenvironmental effects in intact mouse brain tissue.
future_grounding_route: Consider only after a lower-complexity human-cell pilot identifies a reproducible perturbation and a tissue model, barcode delivery route, donor/animal replication plan, and spatial negative controls are fixed.

project_finding_reference.finding_id: spatial and progression intervention direction remain blocked

project_use: External method context for a later tissue-context validation stage, not a current first experiment and not MS evidence.
relationship_note: The method directly addresses cell-niche context but introduces specialized delivery, species, replication, and cost risks that make it a downstream rather than first-line route.

source.citation: Shen et al. Spatial perturb-seq: single-cell functional genomics within intact tissue architecture. Nature Communications. 2026.
source.label: Spatial Perturb-Seq

source_terms.license_or_terms_label: Open-access publisher metadata and short paraphrase
source_terms.reuse_notes: Store bibliographic metadata and a short paraphrase; do not redistribute figures or article text.

why_unverifiable: The project has not reproduced the spatial perturbation technology or tested it in an MS lesion model.
